description:
Provide a reusable inter-frame SIMD LDPC decoder that improves sustained CPU throughput while keeping per-frame convergence and latency explicit.

## Background

The CPU decoder uses floating-point LLRs; placing equivalent message positions from independent frames in adjacent vector lanes can avoid repeated horizontal reductions. The layout must build on canonical edge indexing and prepared workspace. AFF3CT supports multiple SIMD strategies whose batching changes throughput, latency and memory footprint.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Satisfy the [Zen 3 measurement contract](dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md) for correctness, reproducible release benchmarks, comparison validity and adoption; receipts pin its committed version, the frozen protocol and the cell addendum. Include mandatory before/after evidence for production changes and preserve negative outcomes.

- [hard] REQ-07: Produce a reviewed design and worker-sized decomposition after profiling, specifying supported LLR precision, AVX2 lane layout, scalar reference, workspace ownership, per-frame termination, partial batches and integration points before implementation fans out.

- [hard] REQ-08: Expose batch decoding as a reusable gf2-coding API with isolated kernels and thin gf2-sim consumption. Keep converged lanes inactive without altering other frames; preserve input order and results for batch sizes below, equal to and above vector width, including an incomplete final batch.

- [hard] REQ-09: Match the canonical reference under the declared numerical contract across supported worker counts, scheduling, checkpoint/resume, and scalar fallback. Test mixed convergence times and difficult/nonconverging frames so lane masking cannot drop work.

- [hard] REQ-10: Compare single-frame latency, batch-fill cost, sustained throughput and workspace memory against AFF3CT's supported INTRA and INTER modes. Sweep batch sizes and physical-core/SMT configurations; present matched-algorithm results separately from fastest-compatible results.

- [hard] REQ-11: Do not silently introduce quantization or a different update schedule. Any such candidate has a separately reviewed numerical contract and external BER/FER validation with sample counts and confidence intervals before production adoption.

- [hard] REQ-12: Complete a required bounded exploration/decision record for quantized, layered and QC-aware candidates before finalizing implementation scope. Evaluate inter-frame layout against applicable QC intra-frame alternatives without forcing either to win. Numerical-contract review precedes candidate implementation; candidate shipping remains conditional on correctness and measured quality-compatible benefit.

- [hard] REQ-13: Own decoder-specific calibration of batch width, layout selection, small/partial-batch fallback and worker configuration through the canonical offline tuning mechanism. Reconfirm on holdout inputs with batch fill, LLR transposition and workspace costs included; integrate selectors without private threshold copies or a dependency on unrelated core calibration.

- [hard] REQ-14: Define signed-zero/tie behavior, punctured/filler LLR semantics and variable-node accumulation order in the canonical numerical contract. Validate random codewords as well as all-zero words, mixed lane convergence and nonconvergence; quantized candidates specify scaling and saturation, and changed schedules preserve the declared quality bounds rather than claiming bit-exact equivalence without evidence.
title: Vectorize LDPC decoding across frames
